name: Isolani-free open centre

plans.label: Central outpost
plans.description: With no pawn tension to calculate, piece placement is the game: plant a knight on a central square an own pawn still guards.

success.note: A White knight occupies d5 or e5 as a Tabiya-detected outpost.

plans.label: Own the open central file
plans.description: Put a rook on the open central file and keep the opposing rooks off it, so the file becomes an entry square rather than a trading post.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Seize the open file', whose success was a placement contest with no square to test. It is now ownership of the contest: the central file is still open, White has a rook on it, and Black has none. The vocabulary cannot count two rooks, so doubling is not distinguished from a single uncontested rook. Original success note: 'File ownership is a piece-placement contest with no single square to test.'

plans.label: Central outpost
plans.description: The same contest from the other side: a knight on a guarded central square outweighs a nominally freer bishop.

success.note: A Black knight occupies d4 or e4 as a Tabiya-detected outpost.

plans.label: Trade the queens with the file still open
plans.description: Challenge the open file and trade the heavy pieces on it, steering toward the level ending symmetry promises: both queens leave the board while the file stays open.

success.note: RESTATED PLAN. The plan was 'Neutralize the file', whose success was measured in trades and time. It is now the trade the plan is really asking for: both queens are off the board while a central file is still open. The trigger requires both queens present, so this is a real state change rather than a fact about the root. Original success note: 'Neutralization is measured in trades and time, not in one position's arithmetic.'

watch: Whose rooks reach the open central file first.
Whether any central outpost square survives for a knight.
The wing pawn majorities that decide the ending once the pieces come off.
typicalMistakes: Conceding the open file while planning to challenge it later.
Posting a bishop where a knight belongs and vice versa.
Trading into a wing-majority ending without counting whose majority runs faster.

sources: UNGROUNDED: agent-authored strategic claims with no citation, engine evaluation, corpus frequency, or owner review; open-centre doctrine rendered from model knowledge.

Trigger narrowing: 'open centre' here means at least one fully pawnless central file with both queens still on (queens distinguish this family from the symmetrical-queenless entry) and no IQP catalogue match ('isolani-free'). Centres that are open in the practical sense but keep one mobile pawn per side on the central files do not fire; the vocabulary has no notion of pawn tension or mobility.

Degenerate guard added 2026-08-15: the trigger previously fired on the census instrument's `queens_only` board (two kings and two queens, no pawns at all), because `open_file` reads as true on a file with no pawns on it. A clause requiring at least one pawn somewhere on the board was added. Measured before and after: corpus firings 1 of 694 (the single trajectory-qgd-exchange-minority spine position) in both runs; degenerate firings [queens_only] -> [].
